parsed.explanation: The combined regime imposes tier-1 universal exposures: every trans visitor crosses a border system that issues only M/F markers, flags document/sex discrepancies, and can treat suspected misrepresentation as material fraud with possible lifetime ineligibility; visitors have already been blocked or stranded. Facility access is criminalised in the division (birth-sex rule reaching hospitals and restaurants, up to a year's jail) and restricted across many state/provinces, with a documented arrest in a capitol restroom and a 24-hour men's-ward holding. Custody harms are documented (immigration-detention abuse, corrections policies). Mitigation is partial and contested: courts have enjoined some measures, litigation is active, hate-crime statutes exist, but no remedy shown to reliably protect a visitor. Above 0.25-tier organised targeting; below 0.55 because criminal exposure plus state threat-framing reaches routine travel.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-marker passport regime; X markers stopped; discrepancies trigger refusal and potential fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; documented confiscations stranding travellers; trans-athlete entry bans; allied governments issued travel advisories after detentions of foreign nationals over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; ACLU suit ongoing; fraud finding requires four elements, waiver possible, never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Division-issued credentials may mismatch national passport markers, deepening entry screening exposure; state/provincial document divergence flags visitors for scrutiny.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men; corrections bureau adopted hormone-withdrawal and forced-conversion-style policies for inmates; number of trans prisoners no longer reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented for visitors; litigation unresolved.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate to investigation, detention and birth-sex placement with documented abuse patterns.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division criminalises birth-sex-mismatched restroom/changing use in government buildings and public-facing private businesses including hospitals, effective 1 July 2026, first offence up to one year; documented capitol arrest with handcuffing and men's-ward holding; facilities bans in many state/provinces, 4 with criminal exposure.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Constitutional suit filed pre-effect; one district-court narrowing reported but status uncertain; ~30 state/provinces with no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Hospital facilities rule interacts with emergency care exposure; criminal trigger requires refusal to depart, per statutory text.

care_services.exposure: Care bans for minors in 27 state/provinces; proposed national insurance bar; hospitals subpoenaed for under-19 records; lifeline youth services shut down.
care_services.protection: Several orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists; division prisoners may receive hormones per 2024 ruling.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor or parent could become an investigated subject; care-seeking can surface identity to officials.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State framing of gender ideology as extremist; counterterrorism strategy targeting 'radically pro-transgender' groups; schools-directed criminal prosecution threats; 2023 wave of anti-trans bills; public opinion majority favours birth-sex documents.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Statements disclaim targeting mere disagreement; employment-discrimination protection nationally under 2020 ruling; hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile federal framing licenses state-level enforcement and raises outing consequences for visibly trans visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling with a trans minor: care effectively unavailable in much of the country; disclosure-to-parents laws; prosecution threats against facilitators; records subpoenas.
minors_guardians.protection: Several minor-care orders enjoined; three state/provinces protective; local ordinances cover ~40% of division population.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's identity can be disclosed to authorities or institutions during ordinary school, medical or travel encounters.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented as materially above general homicide rate for this division; airport screening reliably risks outing via pat-downs and scanners.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute nationally; 23 state/provinces bias statutes; documented recourse in some state/provinces.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police stop-and-check can force outing via documents; arrest precedent shows police act on facility laws.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Misdemeanour-vs-felony classification unresolved; enforcement status of July 2026 law against visitors undocumented — absence of evidence is not safety; broader 'sex definition' policies may reach beyond mapped bans.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, injunctions on several national measures, ombuds-style legal-aid resources, functioning courts that have granted relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Operative rules shift with litigation outcomes; a visitor cannot predict which regime applies at travel time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Both feature universal, entry-based exclusion/detention exposure with weak remedies; here the register-style targeting is less total than Vellandra's, but custody abuse and criminal facility laws add severity, placing this jurisdiction slightly above that anchor.

Kestrel Isles shows secondary screening and possible refused entry but no criminal statute. Here the division criminalises restroom use in hospitals and restaurants with jail exposure and a documented arrest — materially worse, below 0.55.

Meridia offers trained border officers, functioning tribunal remedies and brief detention. This jurisdiction lacks reliable working remedies, has state threat-framing and custody abuse, so it sits well below 0.75.

Ostravia's birth-sex prison placement and cross-dressing statute resemble elements here, but Ostravia's exposure is custody-centred; this jurisdiction adds universal entry-document exposure plus criminalised private-business facility use, placing it above 0.25.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is defined by a national entry system that structurally exposes every trans visitor (binary markers, discrepancy referral, fraud-ineligibility risk, documented strandings) interacting with division-level criminalisation of facility use reaching hospitals and restaurants, backed by documented arrest practice and state threat-framing. Detention-side abuse is documented, chiefly in immigration and corrections custody into which a document discrepancy can funnel. Protections are real but partial and litigative rather than operative: injunctions, pending suits, hate-crime statutes, and pockets of protective state/provincial law. No organised targeting tier applies, and general violence is not shown trans-elevated, keeping the score above the 0.25 band; but tier-1 universal exposure plus a criminal statute without a demonstrated working remedy keeps it in the Elevated Risk band, around 0.42.
